data.narrative:
Zipline, a Series G autonomous delivery drone operator, is valued at $7.6B post-money on $600M+ raised. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four private and public companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector: Nuro ($6.0B Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B public), Archer Aviation ($3.3B public), and Elroy Air.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier from Series G forward, implies $9.5B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector comparables—Joby, Nuro, and Archer—yields a median valuation of $6.0B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $6.9B. This peer-median method anchors to the lower end of Zipline's current valuation, reflecting median multiples in the broader autonomous vehicle ecosystem.

The triangulated range is $5.1B (low) to $10.9B (high), with a median of $7.8B. This median sits approximately 2% above Zipline's current $7.6B post-money valuation, suggesting current pricing aligns with peer-derived benchmarks. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway clarity for commercial drone delivery, unit economics at scale, and relative competitive positioning within an early-stage, capital-intensive sector where public comparables trade at wide valuation dispersions.
